heroData.title: Hire in France Without a Subsidiary
heroData.subtitle: CDI & Portage Salarial
heroData.description: Navigate strict French labor laws. Use EOR for full-time employees (CDI) or Portage Salarial for freelance-like autonomy with employee benefits.

steps.title: DPAE Filing
steps.description: Déclaration Préalable à l'Embauche filed with URSSAF before start date.

steps.title: Contract (CDI)
steps.description: Contrat de Travail à Durée Indéterminée (Standard permanent contract).

steps.title: Medical Exam
steps.description: Visite d'information et de prévention (VIP) mandatory upon hiring.

steps.title: Health Ins.
steps.description: Mutuelle (private health insurance) enrollment is mandatory (50% employer paid).

items.title: Termination
items.text: Extremely difficult to fire on CDI without 'real and serious cause'. Procedures are strict.

items.title: Période d'Essai
items.text: Trial period (4-8 months for execs) is your only easy exit window. Use it wisely.

rows.label: Management Fee
values: Flat fee per employee. Volume discounts apply.

rows.label: Deposit
values: Refundable deposit of total payroll cost.

faqs.question: What is the difference between EOR and Portage Salarial?
faqs.answer: EOR is a B2B agreement where we become the legal employer. Portage Salarial is a tripartite arrangement specific to France where a freelancer becomes a 'salaried employee' of a portage company to get benefits. EOR is better for long-term hires; Portage is better for autonomous contractors.

faqs.question: Can I hire on a fixed-term contract (CDD)?
faqs.answer: Yes, but French law strictly limits CDD (Contrat à Durée Déterminée) usage to temporary tasks (e.g., replacement, seasonal). You cannot use CDD for regular business activity. The standard is CDI (indefinite).

faqs.question: How does termination work on EOR?
faqs.answer: It is complex. You must have a 'real and serious cause' (performance, economic). We handle the procedure (invitation to meeting, cooling-off period, dismissal letter), but you must strictly follow our guidance to avoid Labor Court (Prud'hommes).

faqs.question: Is the 13th month mandatory?
faqs.answer: Not by law, but it is required by many Collective Bargaining Agreements (CBAs/Conventions Collectives), such as Syntec (Consulting/Tech). We will advise based on the employee's role.

items.title: Lunch Vouchers
items.text: 'Titres-Restaurant' (e.g., Swile) are a beloved perk. Employer pays 50-60%. Almost expected by talent in Paris.

items.title: Right to Disconnect
items.text: Employees have a legal right to ignore emails after hours. Respecting work-life balance (Qualité de Vie au Travail) is taken seriously.

items.title: URSSAF
items.text: The primary agency for collecting social security contributions. Their English portal provides calculators for estimating employer costs. Visit urssaf.fr.

items.title: Service-Public.fr
items.text: The official administration portal for France. Contains definitive guides on 'Contrat de Travail' types (CDI, CDD) and termination procedures. Highly reliable.

items.title: CDI
items.text: Contrat à Durée Indéterminée. The gold standard permanent contract. Hard to terminate.

items.title: Convention Collective
items.text: Collective Bargaining Agreement (CBA). Industry-specific rules that supersede general labor law (e.g., Syntec for IT).

items.title: Cadre
items.text: Executive/Professional status. Comes with higher benefits, pension contributions, and different working hour rules (Forfait Jours).

steps.title: Variables
steps.description: Collect overtime, leave, and expenses (Note de Frais).

steps.title: Calculation
steps.description: Apply CSG/CRDS, healthcare, retirement, and unemployment rates.

steps.title: DSN Filing
steps.description: Submit Déclaration Sociale Nominative by 5th or 15th.

steps.title: Payment
steps.description: SEPA transfer to employees and URSSAF direct debit.

items.title: Complexity
items.text: French payslips are notoriously long. Must show 'Coût Total Employeur' (Total Employer Cost).

rows.label: Full Service
values: Employee support, payments management, leave tracking.

faqs.question: What is the 'Mutuelle' mandatory requirement?
faqs.answer: All private sector employers must provide supplemental health insurance (Mutuelle) and pay at least 50% of the premium. It covers the gap between Social Security regulations and actual medical costs.

faqs.question: How often is the DSN filed?
faqs.answer: The DSN (Déclaration Sociale Nominative) is filed monthly, usually by the 5th or 15th. It aggregates all social data for protecting employees.

faqs.question: What is 'Prélèvement à la Source'?
faqs.answer: It is the Pay-As-You-Earn (PAYE) income tax system. The employer deducts income tax directly from the payslip based on a rate transmitted by the tax authority (DGFiP).

items.title: Remote Work Allowance
items.text: If you require remote work, you may need to pay a small allowance (Indemnité de télétravail) to cover home costs (internet, electricity).

items.title: Net-Entreprises
items.text: The central hub for filing the DSN (Déclaration Sociale Nominative). All social declarations pass through this portal.

items.title: Bulletin Officiel (BOSS)
items.text: Bulletin Officiel de la Sécurité Sociale. The 'Bible' for interpretation of social security laws and contribution bases.

items.title: DSN
items.text: Déclaration Sociale Nominative. Monthly filed data set containing all employee events (pay, sickness, end of contract).

items.title: PAS
items.text: Prélèvement à la Source. Income tax withheld at source by the employer on behalf of the state.

items.title: CSG / CRDS
items.text: Contribution Sociale Généralisée / Contribution au Remboursement de la Dette Sociale. Taxes deducted from gross salary to fund social benefits.

sections.title: Understanding Payslips
sections.subtitle: From Gross to Net
sections.description: How the calculation flow works in the French system.

steps.title: Start with Gross
steps.description: Base salary (`Salaire Brut`) stated in the employment contract.

steps.title: Employer Charges
steps.description: Add ~45% for social security, paid by employer ON TOP of Gross.

steps.title: Employee Charges
steps.description: Deduct ~22% from Gross for employee social contributions.

steps.title: Income Tax (PAS)
steps.description: Deduct 'Prélèvement à la Source' based on tax bracket to get Net Payable.

items.title: Employer Charges
items.text: Adding ~42-45% on top of Gross Salary is the standard rule of thumb for budgeting in France.

items.title: 13th Month
items.text: Many collective agreements (Syntec) require a 13th-month salary payment or holiday bonus.

faqs.question: Why is the gap between Gross and Total Cost so big?
faqs.answer: France funds its high-quality healthcare, pension, and unemployment systems through employer contributions (~45%).

faqs.question: Does this include Income Tax?
faqs.answer: No. Employer cost includes social charges. Income tax is deducted from the employee's Net Salary (PAS).

faqs.question: What is the net take-home pay?
faqs.answer: The net take-home pay is the amount after all social charges and income tax (PAS) have been deducted from the gross salary.

heroData.title: Open a Company (SAS/SARL)
heroData.subtitle: Business Registration
heroData.description: SAS (Société par Actions Simplifiée) is the preferred choice for startups/investors. SARL is for small businesses.

steps.title: Statuts
steps.description: Draft and sign Articles of Association.

steps.title: Capital Deposit
steps.description: Deposit share capital in a blocked bank account (attestation needed).

steps.title: Guichet Unique
steps.description: File application via the INPI 'Guichet Unique' portal.

steps.title: K-Bis
steps.description: Receive K-Bis extract (official company ID) and SIREN number.

items.title: SAS vs SARL
items.text: Choose SAS for flexible dividends and if you plan to raise VC money. President of SAS is 'Assimilé Salarié' (General/Social regime).

faqs.question: Can a foreigner be the President of an SAS?
faqs.answer: Yes. You do not need to be a French resident to be President. However, if you plan to work in France as President, you need a visa/residence permit.

faqs.question: What is the minimum share capital?
faqs.answer: Technically €1, but banks often require a more respectable amount (e.g., €1,000 - €5,000) to open a professional account.

faqs.question: Do I need a physical address?
faqs.answer: Yes, you need a 'Siège Social'. You can use a Domiciliation Company (sedomicilier.fr, Sofradom) for ~€30/month if you don't have an office.

items.title: Guichet Unique (INPI)
items.text: The 'One-Stop Shop' for all business formalities. Since 2023, it replaces the old CFE centers for creation, modification, and cessation of companies.

items.title: Infogreffe
items.text: The commercial court registry. Use this to search for companies, download K-Bis extracts, and check the legal standing of partners.

items.title: K-Bis
items.text: The official ID card of a company. Proves legal existence. Needed for opening bank accounts.

items.title: SIREN / SIRET
items.text: SIREN is the 9-digit company ID. SIRET is the 14-digit location ID (SIREN + 5 digits for the specific office).

items.title: Code APE / NAF
items.text: Activity code assigned by INSEE (e.g., 6201Z for programming). Determines which Collective Agreement applies.

heroData.title: Recruitment (Cabinet de Recrutement)
heroData.subtitle: Cadres & Tech
heroData.description: High demand for engineers. 'Cadre' status (executive/pro) commands higher benefits and notice periods.

steps.title: Sourcing
steps.description: Leverage LinkedIn and APEC (for executives). Agencies are common for niche tech roles.

steps.title: Interviews
steps.description: Process is often formal. Assess cultural fit and technical skills (tests are standard).

steps.title: Promesse d'Embauche
steps.description: A written offer letter. Once signed by both, it is legally binding even before the full contract.

steps.title: Contract Signing
steps.description: Sign the CDI/CDD. Must occur latest by the first day of work.

faqs.question: What is the 'Période d'Essai'?
faqs.answer: It's the trial period. For 'Cadres' (executives/engineers), it is typically 4 months, renewable once (total 8 months). During this time, termination is much easier.

faqs.question: What is 'Préavis' (Notice Period)?
faqs.answer: The notice period for resigning or dismissal. For Cadres, it is usually 3 months. This makes hiring a bit slower as candidates have long notice periods.

faqs.question: Are non-competes enforceable?
faqs.answer: Only if they are limited in time and space, indispensable to protect company interests, AND include financial compensation (normally 30-50% of salary) paid to the employee during the non-compete period.

items.title: France Travail (Pôle Emploi)
items.text: The national employment agency. You can post ads here for free. It is also where you report hiring via DPAE if not automated.

items.title: APEC
items.text: Association pour l'Emploi des Cadres. Specific job board and resource center for hiring executives (Cadres). Essential for high-level tech recruitment.

items.title: Paris (Île-de-France)
items.text: The heart of French tech. Highest salaries, deepest talent pool, but highest cost of living. Station F is here.

items.title: Lyon (Auvergne-Rhône-Alpes)
items.text: Second largest economic hub. Strong in biotech and industry. Salaries are ~10-15% lower than Paris.

items.title: Bordeaux & Nantes
items.text: Atlantic coast hubs attracting many Parisians seeking quality of life. Growing digital ecosystems with vibrant communities.

heroData.title: SIRH Platforms
heroData.subtitle: HR Management
heroData.description: Tools like PayFit, Lucca, and Factorial. Critical for tracking RTT (days off) and sick leave.

steps.title: Data Migration
steps.description: Import employee data (NIR, address, bank details) from spreadsheets.

steps.title: DSN Setup
steps.description: Connect platform to Net-Entreprises for automated DSN declarations.

steps.title: Leave Policy
steps.description: Configure RTT (Réduction du Temps de Travail) and CP (Congés Payés) accrual rules.

faqs.question: Is an HRIS mandatory?
faqs.answer: No, but it is highly recommended once you have >5 employees. Manually tracking leave (Congés Payés), RTT, and sick leave in Excel is prone to errors that can lead to labor disputes.

faqs.question: Does the HRIS handle the DSN?
faqs.answer: Yes, modern tools like PayFit or Lucca automatically generate and file the DSN (Déclaration Sociale Nominative) with Urssaf, saving hours of admin work.

faqs.question: What is the cost per employee?
faqs.answer: Expect to pay €20-€40 per employee per month for a comprehensive solution (Payroll + Leave Management + Onboarding).

items.title: Data Privacy
items.text: Employee data (NIR, health info) is sensitive. Ensure your HRIS is GDPR compliant and servers are in the EU. You must maintain a register of processing activities.

items.title: CNIL
items.text: Commission Nationale de l'Informatique et des Libertés. The regulator for data privacy. Their site offers guides on GDPR compliance for HR data.

rows.label: Congés Payés (CP)
values: Accrues at 2.08 days/month. Must be taken within the ref period.

rows.label: RTT (Réduction Temps Travail)
values: Compensatory days for working >35h/week under forfait jours.

rows.label: Sick Leave (Arrêt Maladie)
values: Employer pays complement after IJSS (Social Security). Check CCN.

rows.label: Maternity (Maternité)
values: 6 before birth, 10 after. Fully paid via Social Security.

rows.label: Paternity (Paternité)
values: Plus 3 days 'naissance'. Mandatory 4 days after birth.

rows.label: Mutuelle (Health Insurance)
values: Mandatory private health top-up. You must offer a compliant plan.

rows.label: Transport (Navigo)
values: Mandatory reimbursement of public transport pass in Île-de-France.

rows.label: Prévoyance (Death/Disability)
values: Often mandatory via Collective Agreement (Convention Collective).

rows.label: Tickets Restaurant
values: 50-60% employer paid. Exempt from social charges up to limits.

rows.label: Forfait Mobilités Durables
values: Tax-free allowance for cycling/scooters/carpool to work.

rows.label: Télétravail Allowance
values: Flat-rate for home office expenses. Common post-COVID.

rows.label: Intéressement/Participation
values: Profit-sharing schemes. Tax-advantaged if kept in PEE plan.

heroData.title: Expert-Comptable
heroData.subtitle: Tax & Books
heroData.description: Only a certified 'Expert-Comptable' can sign off on your Bilans (Annual Accounts). Highly regulated.

sections.title: Setup Process
sections.subtitle: Working with an Expert-Comptable
sections.description: How to initiate and manage the relationship.

steps.title: Lettre de Mission
steps.description: Sign the engagement letter defining the scope (bookkeeping, tax, payroll) and fees.

steps.title: Bank Connection
steps.description: Connect your pro bank account for automated flow of transaction data.

steps.title: Expense Policy
steps.description: Define process for expense reports (`Notes de frais`). Digital receipt storage is legally valid.

steps.title: VAT Cycle
steps.description: Establish monthly VAT transmission. The accountant validates, you approve payment.

rows.label: Annual Closing
values: One-time fee for year-end financial statements (Bilan).

faqs.question: What is an Expert-Comptable?
faqs.answer: A state-certified chartered accountant. In France, only an Expert-Comptable can legally sign off on your annual financial statements (liasse fiscale). You cannot just use an uncertified bookkeeper.

faqs.question: Can I do my own accounting?
faqs.answer: Technically yes, but the risk of error with French tax codes (CGI) is massive. It is standard practice to hire a firm.

faqs.question: What is the FEC file?
faqs.answer: The Fichier des Écritures Comptables (FEC) is a standardized digital file of all accounting entries. You MUST be able to produce this immediately to a tax auditor.

items.title: Closing Date
items.text: Most companies close on Dec 31, but you can choose any date (e.g., Mar 31). Changing it later is possible but requires a formality.

items.title: Ordre des Experts-Comptables
items.text: The regulatory body for accountants. You can verify if a firm is legitimately registered on their directory. Essential for avoiding fraud.

items.title: FEC File
items.text: The Fichier des Écritures Comptables (FEC) must be provided in a specific digital format. If it's non-compliant, you can be fined starting at €5,000.

items.title: Audit Window
items.text: Authorities can audit your accounts for the previous 3 years. Ensure all receipts and bank statements are archived digitally for at least 10 years.

items.title: Droit à l'erreur
items.text: Under the ESSOC law, companies have a 'right to error' for first-time mistakes if they act in good faith and correct them promptly.

steps.title: CSE Election
steps.description: Keep record if you pass 11 employees for 12 months.

steps.title: Document Unique
steps.description: Risk assessment document (DUERP) updated annually.

steps.title: Medical Visits
steps.description: Schedule 'Visite de Reprise' after long sick leave.

faqs.question: What is the CSE?
faqs.answer: Comité Social et Économique. Mandatory if you have >= 11 employees for 12 consecutive months. It represents employee interests.

faqs.question: What is the 'Document Unique'?
faqs.answer: The DUERP is a mandatory risk assessment document listing all potential hazards in the workplace (even stress/burnout). Failure to have it = €1,500 fine.

faqs.question: Are medical exams mandatory?
faqs.answer: Yes. A 'Visite d'Information et de Prévention' (VIP) must happen within 3 months of hiring. Night workers need a stricter exam.

items.title: Affichage Obligatoire
items.text: You must display specific information in the office (Inspector names, emergency numbers, gender equality rules). Digital posting is allowed via intranet.

steps.title: Agreement
steps.description: Employer and employee agree to part ways amicably. No 'cause' needed.

steps.title: Negotiation
steps.description: Agree on severance (indemnité). Minimum is legal statutory severance, but usually higher to incentivize signing.

steps.title: Cooling Off
steps.description: Mandatory 15-calendar-day retraction period where either party can cancel.

steps.title: Homologation
steps.description: Submit to DREETS for approval. They have 15 days to object. If silent, it is approved.

items.title: Eligibility
items.text: Designed for tech workers, researchers, and innovators. Valid for up to 4 years, renewable.

items.title: Family
items.text: The Passeport Talent extends to the spouse and children ("Famille accompagnante"), giving them the right to work immediately.

steps.title: Eligibility Check
steps.description: Ensure the company is eligible (often requires being a 'Young Innovative Enterprise' or recognized by French Tech).

steps.title: Consulate Filing
steps.description: Employee applies at the French consulate in their home country. Must provide contract (Cerfa) and diploma.

steps.title: Arrival & Validation
steps.description: Upon arrival, validate the visa online within 3 months to convert it toward a Residence Permit (Titre de Séjour).

steps.title: Draft Statutes
steps.description: Bank requires the draft Articles of Association (Projet de Statuts).

steps.title: KYC / UBO
steps.description: Proof of ID and address for all Ultimate Beneficial Owners (>25% shares).

steps.title: Capital Deposit
steps.description: Transfer the share capital. Bank issues 'Attestation de dépôt des fonds' needed for registration.

items.title: JEI Status
items.text: Young Innovative Enterprise status offers massive social tax exemptions for R&D staff.

items.title: CIR
items.text: Credit Impôt Recherche - 30% tax credit on R&D spend.

rows.label: CVAE / CFE
values: Local business taxes based on value added or property.

faqs.question: What is JEI (Jeune Entreprise Innovante)?
faqs.answer: A status for startups investing >15% of expenses in R&D. It grants 100% exemption on employer social charges for R&D staff for 7 years. Huge savings.

faqs.question: What is the CFE tax?
faqs.answer: Cotisation Foncière des Entreprises. A local tax based on your office rental value. Even if you have no office (domiciliation), you pay a minimum (~€100-€500/year).

faqs.question: When do I pay VAT (TVA)?
faqs.answer: Monthly or quarterly depending on turnover. You collect 20% on sales and deduct VAT paid on expenses. The difference is paid to Impôts.

items.title: May Deadline
items.text: The 'Liasse Fiscale' (annual return) is typically due in May (for Dec 31 closing). This is crunch time for accountants.

items.title: Impots.gouv.fr
items.text: The portal for all professional tax filings (Espace Professionnel). You access your fiscal account here to pay TVA and IS.

items.title: Bpifrance
items.text: The public investment bank. They manage many innovation grants and soft loans (Prêt d'Amorçage) for startups.

steps.title: Eligibility Check
steps.description: Ensure your R&D tackles 'technological uncertainties' and is not just standard engineering.

steps.title: Track Time
steps.description: Researchers must rigorously track hours spent specifically on R&D tasks.

steps.title: Cerfa 2069-A
steps.description: File this form with your annual IS return. You can offset tax or request a refund (surtout pour PME).

steps.title: Technical File
steps.description: Prepare a scientific dossier justifying the R&D. Essential defense in case of audit (3-year window).

heroData.title: Business Contracts
heroData.subtitle: French Commercial Law
heroData.description: Commercial partners often require strict SLAs and liability caps.

items.title: Disguised Employment
items.text: Treating a contractor like an employee (subordination, fixed hours, single client) leads to reclassification.

items.title: Penalties
items.text: Retroactive social security payments (~45% of all invoices paid), criminal fines for 'concealed work', and potential jail time.

steps.title: Definite Scope
steps.description: Define deliverables, not hours. Pay for results.

steps.title: No Exclusivity
steps.description: Ensure the contractor has other clients.

steps.title: Autonomy
steps.description: Do not provide tools (laptops) or dictate working location/hours.

faqs.question: Can I hire a contractor permanently?
faqs.answer: High risk. If they work full-time for you for years, they may claim employee status. It is better to transition them to EOR or CDI.

faqs.question: Who owns the IP?
faqs.answer: In France, IP transfer is NOT automatic. You must safeguard it with specific 'Cession de droits' clauses listing scope, duration, and territory.

steps.title: Explicit Clause
steps.description: IP does NOT transfer automatically. The contract must explicitly assign rights.

steps.title: Scope Definition
steps.description: Specify the rights being assigned: reproduction, adaptation, distribution, etc.

steps.title: Territory & Duration
steps.description: State 'Monde entier' (worldwide) and 'Durée légale' (legal duration, typically 70 years post-mortem auctoris).

steps.title: Consideration
steps.description: For employees, it is included in salary. For contractors, it must be a separate line item in the invoice/contract.

items.title: Moral Rights
items.text: French authors have inalienable 'droits moraux' (right to be named as author, right to object to distortion). These CANNOT be waived.

items.title: Software Exception
items.text: For software created by employees during work hours, the employer automatically owns the economic rights (Article L113-9 CPI). This does NOT apply to contractors.

items.title: Database Rights
items.text: France recognizes 'sui generis' database rights. If your product is data-heavy, ensure these are also assigned.

items.title: CPI
items.text: Code de la Propriété Intellectuelle. The main legal text governing IP in France.

items.title: INPI
items.text: Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle. Handles trademark and patent registration.

items.title: Cession Exclusive
items.text: Exclusive assignment. Means the original author can no longer use the work themselves.

items.title: Audit Right
items.text: Ensure your MSA includes a right to audit the vendor's security and compliance (GDPR) annually.

items.title: Liability Caps
items.text: Commonly capped at 12 months' fees, but some sectors (Fintech) demand higher caps for data breaches.

heroData.title: French Tech
heroData.subtitle: Station F & Startups
heroData.description: Vibrant ecosystem. 'La French Tech' initiative supports digital growth.

items.title: Station F
items.text: World's largest startup campus in Paris.

steps.title: Paris (Ile-de-France)
steps.description: Home to Station F, AI research labs (Meta, Google), and the majority of VC funding.

steps.title: Sophia Antipolis
steps.description: Europe's leading science park near Nice. Strong for biotech, hardware, and deep tech.

steps.title: Lyon (French Tech One)
steps.description: Strong ecosystem for software, cleantech, and life sciences.

faqs.question: Is English spoken in tech?
faqs.answer: Yes, widely. Most startups in Paris operate in English. However, legal documents must also exist in French (Toubon Law).

faqs.question: Are paying in BSPCE popular?
faqs.answer: Yes. BSPCE (Bons de Souscription de Parts de Créateur d'Entreprise) are tax-advantaged stock options for French startups. Highly valued by talent.

items.title: Local Providers
items.text: OVHcloud is the European leader based in France, offering a sovereign alternative to AWS/GCP for sensitive data.

items.title: Sovereign Cloud
items.text: Required for many government and public sector contracts in France (SecNumCloud certification).

items.title: Scaleway
items.text: Another major French cloud provider popular with startups for its competitive pricing and modern DX.

heroData.title: Digital Agencies
heroData.subtitle: Paris & Lyon
heroData.description: Sophisticated market. SEO and Content Marketing are mature.

sections.title: Hiring an Agency
sections.subtitle: Process for Success
sections.description: Navigate the agency selection process in France effectively.

steps.title: Define Brief
steps.description: Clearly outline scope, budget, and KPIs (e.g., Leads vs Brand Awareness) in a 'Cahier des Charges'.

steps.title: Shortlist & Pitch
steps.description: Select 3-5 agencies. Review portfolios (`références`) and request a strategic proposal.

steps.title: Negotiate
steps.description: Discuss retainer fees vs performance bonuses. Ensure IP rights for created assets transfer to you.

steps.title: Onboarding
steps.description: Set up communication channels (Slack/Teams) and reporting cadence (monthly is standard).

items.title: GDPR Compliance
items.text: CNIL (Data Protection Authority) is strict. Ensure all campaigns and tracking pixels are fully compliant.

items.title: Localization
items.text: Adapt content culturally, don't just translate. French consumers value high-quality, nuanced copywriting.

items.title: Mobile First
items.text: High mobile penetration. Ensure all landing pages and ads are optimized for mobile experiences.

faqs.question: How long are agency contracts?
faqs.answer: Typically 6 to 12 months. 30-day cancellation notices are standard.

faqs.question: Is August really dead?
faqs.answer: Yes. Startups and agencies slow down significantly from July 15 to Aug 25. Avoid launching major campaigns then.
